title: Win-Back: Customers Who Returned After 90-Day Dormancy
description:
Find customers who had a gap of **more than 90 days** between two consecutive orders (they 'churned' and then returned). Return each qualifying customer once.

**Table: orders** — `order_id`, `customer_id`, `customer_name`, `order_date`

Output columns: `customer_id`, `customer_name`. Order by `customer_id`.
solution_sql: WITH order_gaps AS (SELECT customer_id, customer_name, order_date, order_date - LAG(order_date) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date) AS gap_days FROM orders) SELECT DISTINCT customer_id, customer_name FROM order_gaps WHERE gap_days > 90 ORDER BY customer_id;

test_cases.description: Alice (Feb→Jun gap=121 days), Charlie (Jan→May gap=121 days), Diana (Feb→Nov gap=274 days) win-back; Bob all gaps <90; Eve has only one order

hints: Use LAG(order_date) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date) then subtract to get gap_days (INTEGER in DuckDB).
Filter WHERE gap_days > 90 to find dormancy gaps.
Use DISTINCT to return each customer once even if they have multiple gaps > 90 days.
explanation: Alice: Jan→Feb gap=31 days (normal), Feb→Jun gap≈122 days (win-back ✓). Bob: all gaps are 31 and 29 days (no churn). Charlie: Jan→May gap≈121 days (win-back ✓). Diana: Jan→Feb gap=31 days, Feb→Nov gap≈274 days (win-back ✓). Eve has only one order and no gap. Three customers qualify.
